title: v2: Client plugin system — make emitters standalone plugins
description:
## What
Refactor Nexus so clients (claude/mcp/codex/opencode/…) are plugins with a stable interface, and allow third parties to ship new clients.

## Scope
- Define plugin interface: resolve(config)->artifacts, emit(artifacts)->writes, markers, cleanup hooks
- Core ships built-in plugins (claude + mcp first); others can be external
- Nix + TS packaging story for plugins
- Compatibility policy + versioning

## Acceptance
- Can install/enable a plugin client without changing Nexus core
- Plugins participate in state hash + cleanup
- Golden tests for built-in plugins still pass

title: v2: Per-client custom injection — allow user-defined files/dirs per client
description:
## What
Let users attach arbitrary repo files per client (templates/snippets/config fragments) without Nexus needing to hardcode every upstream feature.

## Proposal
- programs.nexus.clients.<client>.files = { "relative/path" = { text|source, mode?, executable? } }
- mkRepo enable.clients.<client>.files = [ ... ] (or auto-include all defined for that client)
- Owned-only cleanup + state hash integration

## Acceptance
- Users can declare a file in dotfiles, enable in a repo, and it shows up at the right path
- Supports both inline text and source path/git source
- Test coverage for overwrite + removal

title: v2: project-level env/vars overrides + dotfiles defaults (templating + strictEnv)
description:
Goal: allow per-project variables/env while keeping defaults in dotfiles.

Design:
- Dotfiles define defaults (e.g. programs.nexus.vars and/or per-mcp env defaults).
- mkRepo accepts project-level overrides/additions.
- Merge precedence: project overrides > dotfiles defaults > process env.
- Apply templating pass over MCP args/env (and potentially other emitters) using merged vars.
- strictEnv controls missing-var behavior.
